about: Inputs of project-page/tools/make_race.py. Totals are measured (median of 5, one session); only the split of each total across BFS levels is modelled.

source.note: The session whose numbers the Chapter 3 README table quotes, so the video and the README quote the same milliseconds. A later session, 20260720T012243Z, gives 2,584 ms for the CPU and 18.8x for 48 blocks, so the speedups are one session's values, not constants.

pacing: Per level k: t_k = o + c * n_k, n_k the exact ring size. o = the lane's meter_scene ms divided by the meter scene's levels (CPU: 0). c = (total_ms - levels * o) / pixels, so each lane ends exactly at its measured total. Inside a level, pixels fill linearly with time.
caveats: Only each lane's finish time is measured. How its fill grows in between is a model (see pacing).
GPU totals are kernel time only (no allocation, no host-device copies). The CPU total is the whole cpu_flood_fill call, which also allocates its arrays.
The 8000 x 8000 square is the whole image. The page's own demo square is far smaller, where the CPU wins.
The CPU lane assumes time proportional to pixels visited; the real CPU is probably faster early and slower late.
The 2-block lane's '2 of 24 SMs' is the placement observed for the same kernel in ch02's dual_block JSON (global_sm_ids [0, 2] in every scene), not recorded for this run.

context.note: Not drawn. Printed by make_race.py for the page caption: the uninstrumented 48-block kernel and the end-to-end 48-block run (allocation and both copies included).
